To find the eigenvalues of matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} -5 & 21 \\ 2 & -21 \end{bmatrix}$, we solve the characteristic equation $\det(A - \lambda I) = 0$.

$$\det \begin{bmatrix} -5 - \lambda & 21 \\ 2 & -21 - \lambda \end{bmatrix} = 0$$

$$(-5 - \lambda)(-21 - \lambda) - (21)(2) = 0$$

$$\lambda^2 + 26\lambda + 105 - 42 = 0$$

$$\lambda^2 + 26\lambda + 63 = 0$$

Factoring the quadratic equation:

$$(\lambda + 7)(\lambda + 19) = 0$$

Thus, the eigenvalues are **$\lambda_1 = -7$** and **$\lambda_2 = -19$**.

---

**Finding Corresponding Eigenvectors:**

1. **For $\lambda_1 = -7$:**
Solve $(A - \lambda_1 I)X = 0$, where $X = \begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix}$.

$$\begin{bmatrix} -5 - (-7) & 21 \\ 2 & -21 - (-7) \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} \implies \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 21 \\ 2 & -14 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}$$

From the first row: $2x_1 + 21x_2 = 0 \implies \frac{x_1}{21} = \frac{x_2}{-2}$.

Thus, the eigenvector for $\lambda_1 = -7$ is $X_1 = \begin{bmatrix} 21 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix}$.

2. **For $\lambda_2 = -19$:**
Solve $(A - \lambda_2 I)X = 0$.

$$\begin{bmatrix} -5 - (-19) & 21 \\ 2 & -21 - (-19) \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} \implies \begin{bmatrix} 14 & 21 \\ 2 & -2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}$$

Using the simplified second row: $2x_1 - 2x_2 = 0 \implies x_1 = x_2$.

Thus, the eigenvector for $\lambda_2 = -19$ is $X_2 = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$.
proTip: Always double-check your eigenvalues using the trace (sum of diagonal elements) and determinant properties before calculating eigenvectors.
